ways: Make a gift, where supporting people with mobility needs fits your group’s lawful purposes under New York’s bingo law.
Hold a bingo night for them, where your license and lawful purposes allow the net proceeds to go to them. Ask your city, town or village clerk first.
Tell your players about them: a word from the caller’s chair, or their flyer on the tables.

sources.scope: Mobility Independence Foundation: mission; based in Mount Upton, New York

age.rule: 18 and older. State law makes no exception for children with a parent.

sources.label: New York General Municipal Law, section 486
sources.scope: Section 486: no person under the age of eighteen shall be permitted to play any game of bingo conducted under a license

name: North Carolina
about: North Carolina allows bingo only for charitable organizations with a state Charitable Bingo License. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: North Carolina Alcohol Law Enforcement: Bingo
regulator_note: North Carolina bingo licenses come from the Bingo Administrator at Alcohol Law Enforcement, 919-710-8885.

sources.scope: Bingo: a bingo game is legal only if the charitable organization has a current Charitable Bingo License; Alcohol Law Enforcement's Bingo Administrator licenses and oversees the games

name: North Dakota
about: North Dakota licenses charitable gaming, which includes bingo, through the Attorney General's Gaming Division. The division publishes lists of licensed organizations and gaming sites. We're building a list of days and times with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: North Dakota Attorney General: Gaming
regulator_note: North Dakota charitable gaming is regulated by the Attorney General's Gaming Division. The Attorney General's office is at 701-328-2210.

sources.scope: Gaming Division: regulates, enforces and administers charitable gaming in North Dakota
Gaming Licensees: current lists of licensed gaming organizations and gaming sites

list_label: North Dakota lists of licensed gaming organizations and sites

halls.money_note: Net proceeds must be paid out within the time set by rule, only for educational, charitable, patriotic, fraternal, religious or public-spirited uses, often as gifts to recipients that use them that way.

sources.scope: N.D.C.C. 53-06.1-11.1 (Games of Chance Laws, effective August 1, 2025): eligible uses of net proceeds
N.D. Admin. Code 99-01.3-14: disbursing net proceeds to recipients

name: Ohio
about: Ohio has its own free bingo finder with game days and times, from the same team.
list_label: Ohio Attorney General: authorized bingo locations
regulator_label: Ohio Attorney General, charitable bingo
regulator_note: Ohio bingo is licensed by the Ohio Attorney General.

sources.scope: Ohio Bingo Finder: organizer-published game schedules plus the Ohio Attorney General's authorized bingo list
Ohio Attorney General authorized bingo locations

halls.money_note: Veteran, fraternal and sporting groups must give at least 25 percent of their first $330,000 of instant bingo net profit each year, and at least 50 percent of anything above that, to an outside charity or a government unit. Other charities use all of it for their own purposes.

sources.scope: Ohio Adm.Code 109:1-4-21: at least 25% of the first $330,000 of instant bingo net profit, at least 50% above it, distributed to an outside charitable organization or government unit

age.rule: 18 and older.

sources.label: Ohio Revised Code 2915.09
sources.scope: R.C. 2915.09(C)(12) (effective September 30, 2021): a charitable organization may not permit anyone it knows or should know is under 18 to play bingo

name: Oklahoma
about: Oklahoma licenses charity bingo through the ABLE Commission. Hospitals, nursing homes and senior centers that host bingo for residents can get an exemption. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: Oklahoma ABLE Commission: Charity Games License Guide
regulator_note: Oklahoma charity games licenses, including bingo, come from the Alcoholic Beverage Laws Enforcement (ABLE) Commission, 405-521-3484.

sources.scope: Charity Games License Guide: license types for charity games, with exemptions for facilities such as hospitals, nursing homes and senior centers that host bingo for residents
ABLE Commission headquarters, main line 405-521-3484

name: Oregon
about: Oregon licenses charitable bingo through the Department of Justice. The state does not publish when games are played, so this list starts with games that groups and senior centers publish themselves.
regulator_label: Oregon Department of Justice: Charitable Gaming
regulator_note: Oregon bingo licenses come from the Department of Justice's Gaming Section, 971-673-1880.

sources.scope: Charitable Gaming: instructions and applications for bingo, raffle and Monte Carlo licenses; Gaming Section phone 971-673-1880

hours_note: Game days come from each place's own published schedule. Call ahead to confirm.

age.rule: 18 and older, or younger when a parent or legal guardian is there to see the cards bought.

sources.label: Oregon Department of Justice, Charitable Gaming FAQs
sources.scope: Bingo cards and raffle tickets may not be sold to persons under 18 unless the parent or legal guardian witnesses the sale

name: Pennsylvania
about: Pennsylvania bingo licenses come from each county, so there is no statewide list of games. We're building one from places that publish their own schedules, with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: How county bingo licenses work (Cumberland County example)
regulator_note: In Pennsylvania, bingo licenses are issued by each county treasurer's office.

sources.scope: "Bingo licenses are issued through your County Treasurer's office." No list of games
Example of an organizer-published schedule; each listing names its own source

hours_note: Game days come from each place's own published schedule. Call ahead to confirm.

halls.money_note: Money from bingo must support the nonprofit purposes of the association that holds the license; a county can revoke a license if it is used for anything else.

sources.scope: 10 P.S. 306: revocation where bingo funds are used for a purpose that does not support the association’s nonprofit purposes

age.rule: 18 and older, or younger with an adult.

sources.label: Pennsylvania Bingo Law, section 5(c)(1), from the Delaware County Treasurer (bingo licensing)
sources.scope: Bingo Law section 5(c)(1) (10 P.S. 305): no person under the age of 18 shall be permitted to play bingo unless accompanied by an adult

name: Rhode Island
about: Rhode Island licenses bingo through the State Police Charitable Gaming Unit. After state approval, the group gets its license from the city or town. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: Rhode Island State Police: Charitable Gaming Unit
regulator_note: Rhode Island bingo is licensed and regulated by the Superintendent of State Police through the Charitable Gaming Unit, 401-764-5568.

sources.scope: Charitable Gaming Unit: helps groups apply for authorization to hold charitable gaming and enforces the charitable gaming law
Rules and Regulations Governing Bingo (270-RICR-50-00-2): which organizations may conduct bingo and how games are approved

name: South Carolina
about: South Carolina allows nonprofit charitable organizations to run bingo under a license from the Department of Revenue. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: South Carolina Department of Revenue: Bingo
regulator_note: South Carolina bingo licenses come from the Department of Revenue, 803-898-5393.

sources.scope: Bingo: nonprofit charitable organizations licensed by the department may operate bingo games; phone 803-898-5393

name: South Dakota
about: South Dakota has no state bingo license. State law lets veterans, religious, charitable, educational, fraternal and civic groups and volunteer fire departments run bingo after giving written notice to the county or city where they play. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: South Dakota law on bingo (SDCL 22-25-25)
regulator_note: For questions about a game, contact the county or city government where it is held.

sources.scope: South Dakota Codified Law 22-25-25: bingo is permitted for listed organizations under set conditions, including thirty days of written notice to the county or municipality

name: Tennessee
about: Tennessee does not license weekly bingo. Under the Tennessee Nonprofit Gaming Law, an eligible nonprofit can hold a yearly game-of-chance fundraising event, and bingo is one of the games allowed. The Secretary of State's office takes the applications and has a search for the events.
regulator_label: Tennessee Secretary of State: Charitable Gaming Event FAQs
regulator_note: Questions go to the Secretary of State's Charitable Solicitations office, 615-741-2555.

sources.scope: Charitable Gaming Event FAQs: eligible 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(19) organizations may hold an annual game of chance event after filing an application; authorized games include raffles, reverse raffles, cakewalks, cake wheels and bingo; phone 615-741-2555

name: Texas
about: Texas licenses charitable bingo statewide, and the state's Bingo Hall Locator lists each licensed hall with its days and times.
hours_note: Hours are the licensed bingo times from the Texas Bingo Hall Locator. Call ahead to confirm before you go.
regulator_label: Texas charitable bingo (txbingo.org)
regulator_note: Texas bingo was regulated by the Texas Lottery Commission until 2025, when the Legislature moved it to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. The bingo line is 800-246-4677.

sources.scope: Texas State Law Library: Senate Bill 3070 (2025) abolished the Lottery Commission and moved bingo licensing to the Department of Licensing and Regulation, whose bingo site offers "find a bingo hall near you"
Charitable bingo site: contact line 800-BINGO-77 (800-246-4677)
Charitable bingo home page: "Where can I play?" opens the state bingo hall locator

halls.money_note: A licensed group must put its net proceeds from bingo toward its own charitable purposes.

sources.scope: Texas Occupations Code 2001.454: net proceeds devoted to the charitable purposes of the organization

age.rule: 18 and older, or younger with a parent or guardian. A hall may post a notice keeping people under 18 out.

sources.label: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, Charitable Bingo: Players (Occupations Code 2001.418)
sources.scope: A person younger than 18 may not play bingo unless accompanied by a parent or guardian; a license holder may bar players under 18 by posted notice

name: Utah
about: Utah does not license bingo, and state law does not allow gambling. The bingo we list in Utah is free bingo at senior centers. We're building the list with help from centers and players.
hours_note: Game days come from each center's own published schedule. Call ahead to confirm.
regulator_label: Utah Code: gambling (section 76-9-1402)
regulator_note: Utah has no bingo regulator. State law prohibits gambling, so the places listed here offer bingo free of charge.

sources.scope: Utah Code 76-9-1402, participating in gambling: the section states it acts as the state's prohibition of gambling
Example of a county senior center games page listing free bingo; each listing names its own source

age.rule: No age in state law: Utah bans gambling, so there is no paid charity bingo. The bingo listed here is free, at senior centers.

sources.label: Utah Constitution, Article VI, Section 27
sources.scope: Games of chance not authorized: the Legislature shall not authorize any game of chance, lottery or gift enterprise under any pretense or for any purpose

sources.label: Utah Code 76-9-1402
sources.scope: Participating in gambling is a misdemeanor; the section acts as the state’s prohibition of gambling

name: Vermont
about: Vermont has no state bingo license. State law lets nonprofit organizations run games of chance, including bingo, to raise money for charitable, religious, educational and civic work. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: Vermont law on nonprofit games of chance (13 V.S.A. § 2143)
regulator_note: No state office licenses bingo in Vermont.

sources.scope: 13 V.S.A. § 2143: a nonprofit organization may run lotteries, raffles or other games of chance to raise funds for charitable, religious, educational and civic undertakings; the section also sets limits on bingo games

name: Virginia
about: Virginia's Office of Charitable and Regulatory Programs publishes a directory of bingo sessions, with the days and the times the doors open and close. Games marked "in the social quarters" may be for members and their guests, so call first.
hours_note: Hours are when the doors open and close, from Virginia's directory of bingo sessions. Call ahead to ask when the first game starts.
regulator_label: Virginia Office of Charitable and Regulatory Programs: Charitable Gaming
regulator_note: Virginia charitable gaming permits come from the Office of Charitable and Regulatory Programs at the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. Its complaint line is 804-371-0498.

sources.scope: Charitable Gaming: the office issues charitable gaming permits and regulates the games; links to the online directory of bingo sessions, updated monthly; complaint line 804-371-0498
Registered Gaming Activity, September 2026: bingo sessions by locality with addresses, days, and doors-open and doors-close times

halls.money_note: Groups must use at least 10 percent of their gross receipts (20 percent of electronic gaming adjusted gross receipts) for their religious, charitable, community or educational purposes. Those payments may go to scholarship funds or to religious, charitable, educational or community causes.

sources.scope: 11VAC20-20-20: minimum use of proceeds, 10% of gross receipts and 20% of electronic gaming adjusted gross receipts
11VAC20-20-110: use of proceeds payments may be made for scholarship funds or religious, charitable, educational or community purposes

age.rule: 18 and older, or younger with a parent or legal guardian. Instant bingo, pull tabs, seal cards and network bingo are for 18 and older only.

sources.label: Virginia Administrative Code, 11VAC20-20-60
sources.scope: 11VAC20-20-60(C): individuals younger than 18 may play bingo when accompanied by a parent or legal guardian; 11VAC20-20-60(F): no one younger than 18 may play or redeem paper instant bingo, pull-tabs, seal cards or network bingo

name: Washington
about: Washington oversees nonprofit bingo through the Washington State Gambling Commission. Its licensee lookup shows which groups hold a bingo license, but not when they play, so this list starts with games the groups publish themselves.
hours_note: Game days come from each place's own published schedule. Call ahead to confirm.
regulator_label: Washington State Gambling Commission
regulator_note: Washington bingo is overseen by the Washington State Gambling Commission.

sources.scope: Washington State Gambling Commission: its oversight includes nonprofit raffles and bingo
Look up an organizational or individual licensee: search the list of approved licensees

halls.money_note: Bingo must be run by the group itself, and no part of the proceeds may benefit anyone other than the group running the game. After the necessary costs of the games, all net income must go to the lawful purposes the group stated when it applied for its license. Running a game for the benefit of specific named recipients needs the Gambling Commission’s approval first.

sources.scope: RCW 9.46.0205: bingo defined; no part of the proceeds may inure to anyone other than the group conducting the game
WAC 230-07-010: net gambling income only for the lawful purposes stated in the license application; activities for named recipients need prior approval

partner.name: Light Upon Light
partner.about: Light Upon Light is a Washington nonprofit, led by a differently-abled founder, that works for accessibility, education and equality for differently-abled people through education, advocacy, mentorship and community programs.
ways: Tell your players about them: a word from the caller’s chair, or their flyer on the tables.
Make a gift from money that is not bingo proceeds, or invite your members to give on their own.
Volunteer, or invite them to speak to your members.
partner.note: Washington law keeps bingo proceeds with the group that runs the game, so we never ask for a share of bingo money or for a game run for them.

sources.scope: Light Upon Light: 501(c)(3) advocating accessibility, education and equality for differently-abled people
Light Upon Light, Everett, Washington: mission

age.rule: 18 and older, or younger with a parent, grandparent or spouse who is at least 18, or a court-appointed guardian.

sources.label: Washington Administrative Code 230-06-010
sources.scope: WAC 230-06-010: no one under 18 may participate in gambling except licensed bingo when accompanied by an adult member of their immediate family (spouse, parents or grandparents) or a guardian at least 18

name: West Virginia
about: We haven't found a public list of West Virginia bingo games with their days and times, so we're building one from places that publish their own schedules, with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: West Virginia Tax Division: bingo and raffle licenses
regulator_note: West Virginia bingo is licensed by the State Tax Commissioner, 304-558-3333.

sources.scope: Bingo licenses come from the Tax Commissioner; phone 304-558-3333; no list of licensees linked
Example of an organizer-published schedule; each listing names its own source

hours_note: Game days come from each place's own published schedule. Call ahead to confirm.

halls.money_note: All net proceeds must be spent within a year of the license on the charitable or public service purposes named in the application, by giving them to a qualified recipient organization or, with the Tax Commissioner’s approval, on a charitable or public service activity the group sponsors itself.

sources.scope: W. Va. Code 47-20-15: net proceeds spent within one year for the purposes stated in the application; permission to support the group’s own activity
W. Va. Code 47-20-2: definitions, including spending net proceeds by devoting them to a qualified recipient organization

age.rule: 18 and older. Younger people may watch with an adult relative or legal guardian, but may not play.

sources.label: West Virginia Code 47-20-4
sources.scope: 47-20-4: no licensee shall allow anyone under 18 to participate in playing bingo; under 18 may attend with and under the supervision of an adult relative or legal guardian

name: Wisconsin
about: Wisconsin licenses bingo run by charitable organizations through the state Office of Charitable Gaming, and the state's Active Bingo Occasion Search lists every licensed bingo date with its place and start time.
hours_note: Days and start times are worked out from the dated bingo occasions on the state's Active Bingo Occasion Search. Some games are held only on certain weeks. Call ahead to confirm before you go.
list_label: Wisconsin Department of Administration: Active Bingo Occasion Search
regulator_label: Wisconsin Office of Charitable Gaming: Bingo Licenses
regulator_note: Wisconsin bingo licenses come from the Division of Gaming's Office of Charitable Gaming, 608-270-2530.

sources.scope: Bingo License: the Division of Gaming's Office of Charitable Gaming licenses and regulates bingo conducted by charitable organizations; bingo line 608-270-2530
Active Bingo Occasion Search: each licensed bingo occasion with group, place of play, street address, city, ZIP code, date and start time (no phone)

age.rule: 18 and older, or younger when an adult relative or guardian is in the building.

sources.label: Wisconsin Statutes 563.51(13)
sources.scope: 563.51(13)(a): a minor may not play licensed bingo unless an adult relative by blood, marriage or adoption, or the minor’s guardian, is present in the building or on the premises

sources.label: Wisconsin Statutes 990.01(20)
sources.scope: 990.01(20): "minor" means a person who has not attained the age of 18 years

name: Wyoming
about: Wyoming allows bingo only by charitable or nonprofit organizations licensed by the Wyoming Gaming Commission. We haven't found a public list of games, so we're building one with help from halls and players.
regulator_label: Wyoming Gaming Commission: Charitable Gaming
regulator_note: Wyoming bingo licenses come from the Wyoming Gaming Commission, 307-265-4015.

sources.scope: Charitable Gaming: bingo and pull tabs may be conducted only by charitable or nonprofit organizations that have existed in Wyoming for at least three years and are licensed by the Commission; phone 307-265-4015
